test_cases.question: Does GDPR impose additional obligations on providers of publicly available electronic communications services?
test_cases.answer: No. This Regulation shall not impose additional obligations on natural or legal persons in relation to processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union in relation to matters for which they are subject to specific obligations with the same objective set out in Directive 2002/58/EC.
test_cases.supporting_quote: This Regulation shall not impose additional obligations on natural or legal persons in relation to processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union in relation to matters for which they are subject to specific obligations with the same objective set out in Directive 2002/58/EC
key_phrases: public communication networks in the Union

test_cases.question: Under what conditions does GDPR not add extra obligations for electronic communications processing?
test_cases.answer: GDPR does not add extra obligations when: (1) the processing is in connection with publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union; and (2) the matters are already subject to specific obligations with the same objective under Directive 2002/58/EC (the ePrivacy Directive).
test_cases.supporting_quote: in relation to matters for which they are subject to specific obligations with the same objective set out in Directive 2002/58/EC

test_cases.question: Which services fall within the carve-out for matters already subject to obligations under Directive 2002/58/EC?
test_cases.answer: The carve-out covers processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union. This includes telecom providers, ISPs, and similar services operating on public networks.
test_cases.supporting_quote: processing in connection with the provision of publicly available electronic communications services in public communication networks in the Union

b2b_relevance: MEDIUM - Article 95 is critical for B2B SaaS in the telecom/communications sector. Key implications: (1) If you provide publicly available e-comms services (VoIP, messaging platforms, ISPs), ePrivacy may take precedence over GDPR for certain matters, (2) This prevents double regulation where ePrivacy already covers the same objective, (3) For non-telecom B2B SaaS, GDPR applies fully.
